name: 46,XY Difference of Sex Development Due to a Cholesterol Synthesis Defect

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for 46,XY DSD due to Cholesterol Synthesis Defect

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in cholesterol biosynthesis (e.g., DHCR7, SC5D)
Elevated serum sterol precursors and reduced cholesterol levels detected by biochemical assays
Presence of undervirilized external genitalia in 46,XY individuals with ambiguous genitalia or hypospadias
Abnormal gonadal or internal reproductive anatomy on pelvic ultrasound or MRI
Positive family history of cholesterol synthesis defects or related metabolic disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical phenotype plus biochemical abnormalities and genetic confirmation of pathogenic variants in cholesterol synthesis genes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, biochemical, and genetic data due to phenotypic variability.

pathognomonic.notes: Includes micropenis, hypospadias, and labioscrotal fusion abnormalities

pathognomonic.symptomName: Biochemical evidence of impaired cholesterol synthesis with elevated sterol precursors
searchTerms: cholesterol synthesis defect with sterol buildup
impaired cholesterol production with precursor accumulation

common.notes: Common genital anomaly in affected males

searchTerms: urethral opening on underside of penis

common.symptomName: Growth retardation or failure to thrive

common.notes: Reduced muscle tone observed in some patients

occasional.notes: Reported in a subset of patients

rare.notes: Very rare but reported in isolated cases

laboratory: Elevated serum 7-dehydrocholesterol and other sterol precursors
imaging: Pelvic ultrasound showing dysgenetic gonads or absent Müllerian structures
MRI of brain may show structural abnormalities
genetic: Pathogenic variants in DHCR7, SC5D, or other cholesterol biosynthesis genes
other: Family history of cholesterol synthesis defects
Abnormal newborn screening for sterol metabolites in some regions

distinguishingFeatures: Phenotypic female external genitalia despite 46,XY karyotype
Overlapping cholesterol synthesis defect but typically 46,XY with multiple congenital anomalies

redFlags: Severe developmental delay with biochemical evidence of cholesterol synthesis defect
Family history of neonatal death or metabolic disorders
references: Orphanet: 46,XY difference of sex development due to a cholesterol synthesis defect, ORPHA:325511
Miller WL. Disorders in the initial steps of steroid hormone synthesis. J Steroid Biochem Mol Biol. 2017.
Huang N, et al. Genetic basis of disorders of sex development. Nat Rev Endocrinol. 2019.
